subject: Request for Detailed TAM Coverage & Incident Communications — Redwood RFI
messages:
From: Susan Connors <susan.connors@fintrust.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Hall <alex.hall@fintrust.com>, procurement@fintrust.com
Date: 2026-12-20T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: RFP: TAM Coverage & Incident Communications — initial questions

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. As we close out the RFP packet, Procurement has asked for a detailed one-page (or structured table) covering your TAM coverage model, escalation tiers, guaranteed response/ack windows, support hours by region, and a sample incident communication timeline. Specifically: 

- Team composition (TAM vs Support vs Escalation engineer) and on-call rotations
- SLA response/ack windows for Sev 1/2/3 incidents and business hours vs off-hours behavior
- Notification cadence and templates we can expect during an incident (initial, updates, resolution)
- Escalation contacts and path length for urgent issues (phone + email)
- Any regional limitations or blackout windows (maintenance, holidays)

Can you provide the completed document and any sample templates by EOD today? Our internal reviewers want to include these as an RFP appendix.

Appreciate it — Susan
Susan Connors
Director, Strategic Sourcing | FinTrust Bank

Team — forwarding FinTrust's ask (see below). They want a structured one-pager + incident timeline by EOD. Can we assemble the following and confirm ownership?

Ask breakdown / owners: 
- TAM coverage model & staffing (owner: Karthik) — include typical TAM FTE per committed GPU pool size, primary contact vs escalation engineer, and on-call overlap windows.
- SLA tables (owner: Neha) — ack/response/target resolution guidance for Sev1 (platform down), Sev2 (degraded), Sev3 (question/ops). Include business hours (US/EU/APAC) and off-hours routing.
- Incident comms timeline + sample templates (owner: Monica) — initial notice, 30/60/120 min updates, and final RCA cadence. Provide subject lines and short template bodies.

Attachments: I started a template (TAM_Coverage_Template.xlsx) — please update directly and attach final PDF.

Deadline: 15:30 PST today (gives me time to consolidate and send to FinTrust). If any blocker, call me immediately.

Thanks — Priya

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T12:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP: TAM Coverage & Incident Communications — FinTrust (draft attached)

Priya / team — attaching my draft TAM coverage section and an incident timeline spreadsheet. See high-level responses below; details are in the attached files.

Attachment stubs: TAM_Coverage_Draft_v1.pdf (summary), Incident_Notification_Timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet with cadence and recipient lists)

Key points / clarifications: 
- TAM model: Dedicated TAM leads are assigned per Reserved Capacity contract (baseline 1 TAM per 4 Reserved GPU pools). TAM responsibilities: weekly syncs, runbook maintenance, escalation coordination.
- On-call: TAMs are not primary on-call for Sev1 outside business hours; we have a 24/7 platform operations rotation (Ops Escalation Engineer) with a documented handoff process. TAMs cover post-incident follow-up and prioritization during business hours.
- SLAs (ack / initial response windows):
  - Sev 1 (production down): 15 min ack (24/7 pager), 1 hour initial triage update, P0 escalation path if unresolved at 2 hours.
  - Sev 2 (severe degradation): 30 min ack (business hours) / 1 hour off-hours, 4 hour initial triage update.
  - Sev 3 (minor/ops): next business day response.
- Notifications: initial notification within the ack window, then structured updates at 30/60/120 minutes with owners and action items. Final resolution + RCA within 72 hours (preliminary) and 10 business days for full RCA deliverable.
- Escalation path length: typical internal ladder is: On-call Engineer -> Ops Lead -> TAM -> Head of Support -> CTO (phone escalation available at Ops Lead level). We will provide names and primary phone numbers after contract.
- Regional notes: No planned blackout windows; maintenance windows are scheduled with 48-hour notice and will be region-aware (US/EU/APAC). Holidays may increase resolution SLAs slightly — we'll list observed holidays per region in the appendix.

Please review the attached drafts for wording and accuracy. Monica — can you pull together the sample email templates (initial / update / resolution) and drop into the timeline sheet?

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-20T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP: TAM Coverage & Incident Communications — Redwood response (attachments)

Hi Susan / Alex,

Appended please find our completed TAM coverage response and a proposed incident communication timeline for inclusion in your RFP appendix. Key highlights are summarized below; the attached PDF and timeline spreadsheet include the full tables and sample message templates.

Summary highlights: 
- TAM coverage model: One dedicated TAM per four reserved GPU pools; TAM handles proactive reviews, weekly business reviews, and prioritized post-incident follow-up during business hours.
- 24/7 ops: Platform Operations provides 24/7 on-call for Sev1 (15-minute ack), with an escalation ladder that surfaces to TAMs and senior leadership as needed.
- SLA windows: Sev1 = 15 min ack / 1 hr triage update / P0 escalation at 2 hrs. Sev2 = 30 min ack (business hours) / 1 hr off-hours ack / 4 hr triage. Sev3 = next business day.
- Notifications: Initial alert + owner + severity within ack window; status updates at 30/60/120 min; preliminary RCA within 72 hrs; full RCA within 10 business days.
- Contacting us: For urgent matters we provide a dedicated escalation phone line (post-contract) and primary ops pager. Contracting teams often route legacy phone-based escalations through Karthik or Neha.

Attachments included: 
- TAM_Coverage_Response_v1.pdf (one-page structured summary)
- Incident_Notification_Timeline.xlsx (detailed cadence, recipients, and sample templates)

Next steps: Please confirm receipt and advise if you want us to convert the one-pager into your RFP table format (we can do that as a follow-up). Happy to hop on a 30-min call if reviewers want to walk through the timelines.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
